title: Ice Cream Soda, flavors other than chocolate

content.title: About
content.content: Ice cream soda is a carbonated dessert drink that blends a creamy ice‑cream flavor with a light fizz. It is offered in a variety of flavors, excluding chocolate, such as vanilla, strawberry, mint, caramel, and other fruit‑based options.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first recipe for carbonated ice cream appeared in the early 20th century in the United States.
Ice cream soda is often served in glass cups with a straw to preserve the bubbles.
In some countries it is called “fizzy ice cream” or “sparkling ice cream.”
Non‑chocolate flavors are especially popular with children because they are less sweet and more vibrant.
The carbonation is created by adding food‑grade sodium bicarbonate and an acid (e.g., citric acid) that react when the drink is poured.

items.title: Calcium source
items.content: The dairy base provides calcium, essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Certain flavors (e.g., vanilla) contain riboflavin (B2) and cobalamin (B12), supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: The carbonated water component helps maintain fluid balance, especially on hot days.

items.title: Quick energy
items.content: Sugar and lactose supply rapid glucose, useful for a quick energy boost.

items.title: Mood uplift
items.content: Sweet taste and gentle fizz can stimulate serotonin release, improving mood.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Large amounts of sugar can contribute to weight gain and increase the risk of tooth decay.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: The dairy base may cause discomfort for people who cannot digest lactose.

items.title: Carbonation
items.content: Carbonated drinks can cause heartburn or bloating in some individuals.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Allergy to casein or whey requires avoiding the product.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Because of the creamy base and sugar, a serving can be calorie‑rich; moderation is advised.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve ice cream soda chilled, typically in a glass with a straw. You can garnish with fresh berries, mint leaves, or a sprinkle of cinnamon to enhance flavor. Avoid vigorous stirring, which can dissipate the carbonation.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep frozen at –18 °C (0 °F) or lower. After opening, consume within 24 hours to retain fizz. Discard if ice crystals form or the taste changes.
